newsitem.title: USA: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON WITHDRAWS FROM U.S. CHAMPIONSHIPS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON WITHDRAWS FROM U.S. CHAMPIONSHIPS.

text.p: Injured world 200-meter record holder Michael Johnson withdrew from next week's U.S. championships on Thursday, which will leave the athletics world championships in August without one of the sport's marquee names.
"He made the decision after seeing his doctor today," Brad Hunt, Johnson's agent, said in a telephone interview from his office in Boulder, Colorado.
The double Olympic gold medalist severly pulled his left quadriceps in Sunday's match race with Canadian Donovan Bailey and has been unable to work out this week.
Hunt said Johnson still planned to have a European season, and hoped to run in at a meeting in Paris on June 25.
But under American track rules, without competing at the U.S. championships in Indianapolis next week Johnson cannot earn a spot on the U.S. team for the worlds in Athens.
Hunt also said that world long jump record holder Mike Powell would not compete in the U.S. championships because of hip and groin injuries.
Another top U.S. star, decathlon world record-holder Dan O'Brien, withdrew from the Indianapolis meet Tuesday because of an apparent stress fracture.
The three-time world champion also will be ineligible for the world championships in Athens because only the top three finishers in the U.S. championships are eligible for the world team.
The strict U.S. qualifying rules leaves the biggest athetics event of the year without at least three of its brightest stars, world record holders all.
